headline: Oil Prices Soar, Yet Domestic Gas Prices Remain Calm; Government 'Price Control' Dilemma
summary: International oil prices are soaring and global crude inventories are plunging as the Middle East crisis intensifies. Domestic gasoline prices in Korea have been unchanged for 13 days under a government maximum price system.
why: Crude oil is the benchmark input for fuels, petrochemicals and transport costs, so supply shocks in the Middle East feed directly into global energy prices. Price caps in importing countries can decouple retail prices from crude.
why_moved: Input states the Middle East crisis has intensified again, with oil prices soaring and global crude inventories plunging.
